A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same label-smoothing and selective-classification study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, segmentation, distribution-shift, and logit-normalization experiments in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds uncertainty-score comparisons and qualitative segmentation analyses in Appendices E.1 and F.

M1.justification: LS training and post-hoc scoring by the maximum p-normalized logit remain unchanged. v2 corrects the explicit norm formula and explains the omission of centralization, without establishing a changed algorithm or implementation.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ImageNet classification, the ImageNet-plus-Sketch mixture, Cityscapes segmentation, and CIFAR-100 classification. Additional score comparisons and illustrative images use existing coverage; they introduce no distinct task or input environment.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix E.1 adds DOCTOR and entropy across LS levels, and Energy for CE and LS with alpha=0.2, to the ResNet-50/ImageNet comparisons. These supplement the retained MSP and logit-normalization comparisons, with the expansion confined to this setting.

E3.justification: The original splits, training budgets, architectures, preprocessing, and quantitative evaluation protocols are retained. The added qualitative Cityscapes case studies explicitly use p=5 for both CE and LS (Appendix F), supplementing the retained quantitative normalization evaluations with validation-selected p=4 and p=8.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted checks of dependence on uncertainty-score choice (Appendix E.1), another ImageNet error example, and segmentation boundary-error and normalization-failure case studies (Appendix F). The Sketch robustness tests and logit-distribution analyses already appear in v1.

E5.justification: Both use descriptive mean-plus-or-minus-standard-deviation bands over samples, including the same sliding-window procedures. The new relative-distribution panels redisplay this information. Neither version reports repeated training seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Principal benchmark results are retained. v2 adds alternative-score results, including Energy %AURC of 11.27 for CE and 12.57 for LS alpha=0.2 (Figure 18), exact coverage at 1% risk (Figure 1), and qualitative cases. v2 Figure 13 also replaces v1 Figure 12's mIoU-labeled 72.4/72.0 with 5.1/5.2, conflicting with v2 Figure 3; this does not establish a comparable performance decline.

T1.justification: New Appendix C derives the empirical one-hot-loss gradients and separate maximum-logit regularization for correct and incorrect predictions (Equations 19–21). v2 Equation 16 also corrects the p-norm expansion to include absolute values. The population-loss analysis and positive-logit theorem and proof are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: v1 presents LS-induced degradation as something this work reveals; v2 explicitly credits earlier observations and frames the empirical contribution as broader validation, emphasizing dependence on LS strength. The central claims about imbalanced regularization and recovery through logit normalization remain.

C2.justification: v2 expands the distinction between marginal calibration and per-sample uncertainty ranking. Appendix F adds interpretations of boundary errors and explicitly identifies cases where normalization leaves confident errors unresolved. The central mechanism remains the same, with much epistemic-uncertainty language recast in terms of model fit.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.3 specifies the normalization search grid p=1 through 8 and its AURC objective; Section 5 and Appendix E.5 clarify that centralization is omitted. v1's statement that an accompanying CIFAR-10/ResNet-20 demo is provided disappears. Full project code and checkpoints remain promised future releases in both.

R1.justification: v2 substantively repositions the work around Zhu et al. (2022; 2024), acknowledging prior LS/SC observations and emphasizing broader validation and explanation. New Appendix E.5 develops a detailed comparison with Cattelan and Silva's explanation of normalization. This extends well beyond the latter citation's publication update or citation-style changes.

P1.justification: The introduction and explanatory narrative are extensively rewritten. Experimental findings and gradient analysis become separate main sections, experimental details move, and the aleatoric/epistemic exposition is replaced by simpler model-fit language with an appendix note. v2 also adds an appendix contents page and separate reproducibility and ethics statements.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and redesigns many plots with risk-difference or relative-logit panels. Figures are split, combined, and relocated; the segmentation example moves to Figure 1 with a coverage table. New score-comparison and failure-case figures accompany substantial redisplay of existing results.

improvement.justification: v2 more carefully positions its contribution, checks dependence on uncertainty-score choice, adds the one-hot-loss derivation, and documents failures of normalization (Appendices C, E.1, and F). These strengthen and qualify largely unchanged findings. The gains outweigh the localized reporting regression in Figure 13's inconsistent mIoU entries, but do not establish a substantial overall advance.
